text:
alyssa: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression after the last autotuner change. Short seq (<=16) latency up ~15% on some SM86 nodes. Kernel picker is preferring the 'large-tile-tc' path that uses tensor cores even though bf16 path seems degraded.

perf-bot: autotune report for job 2026-03-17T10:12Z:
```
> device: sm_86 (RTX A5000-like)
> probe: tensor_cores=1, bf16_supported=1, fp8_supported=0
> selected_kernel: large-tile-tc (uses DP4A/tc math)
> observed: median token latency 12.5ms (seqlen=8), expected ~10.8ms
> fallback to small-tile-no-tc yields 10.3ms
```

cheng: thanks — I pulled a heap of microbench runs. Looks like kernel cost model uses only peak flops + power of tile size, not taking KV-cache shadowing into account. For short sequences KV cache constantly hits L1 and the tc kernel has poorer launch+sync cost.

mike: can repro locally on a dev A5000 with `--seqlen 8 --batch 4`. Quick hack: forcing `FORCE_TENSORCORE=0` in env drops latency back. Not a long-term fix.

samir: idea: change probe to include a tiny end-to-end microbenchmark that mimics KV warmup and a representative mix of prefix tokens. e.g. do 3 warmup tokens then measure 32 tokens sample and compare kernels. If the ratio > 1.03 pick no-tc path for seqlen<=16.

cheng: I ran a quick comparison of selection heuristics. Short summary:
- current heuristic: score = peak_flops * tile_efficiency - alpha * launch_overhead
- problem: launch_overhead is a constant, not measured per kernel or per seq distribution
- proposed: add `measured_latency_per_kernel[seqlen_category]` and favor measured walltime for representative sequences

perf-bot: new microbench snippet output:
```
> bench: 3warm+32run (simulated kv hits)
> kernel: large-tile-tc -> 38.6ms total (avg token 1.21ms)
> kernel: small-tile-no-tc -> 33.1ms total (avg token 1.04ms)
> ratio(tc/no-tc)=1.165
```

alyssa: good data. Two follow-ups: (1) do we have a safe probe that runs quickly during startup? aim <200ms wall for probe. (2) put a config flag to allow per-deployment override of autotuner decisions for critical customers.

mike: for (1) we can do a parametric microbench: run only 8 tokens with warmup 2 and scale result with a small calibration factor. That keeps probe ~120ms. I'll prototype.

samir: for (2) we already have `runtime.config.autotune_overrides` but it only accepts kernel names. Add an override key `prefer_non_tc_for_seqlen<=X` so ops can force path without editing code.

cheng: also found weirdness: `cudaDeviceGetAttribute` reported `cudaDevAttrTensorCoreMajor` true, but a driver regression on 537.x made fp16->bf16 convert path slower. We should detect driver ABI quirks and add a per-driver penalty in probe.

perf-bot: detected driver 537.34 on node pool-a, flagged known-bug #IF-4321 (bf16 conv slow on tc kernels). Suggest fallback.

alyssa: okay let's do a three-step plan:
1) mike: prototype fast microbench probe and add measured_latency bucket for seqlen categories (<=16, 17-64, >64). target PR by EOD tomorrow.
2) samir: add config key for override + logging of why autotuner chose a path (include measured vs model score).
3) cheng: collect a nightly sweep across all driver versions we run and produce a compatibility matrix (sm, driver, runtime flags) to feed into the autotuner default mapping.

mike: noted. I'll open a draft PR and include results of the small param bench. Will also add an env `AUTOTUNE_DEBUG=1` to dump selection reasons in logs.

cheng: one more: KV cache behavior — if the probe measures with empty cache we bias towards large kernels. Make sure simulated probe uses a warmed prefix pattern typical of chat workloads. I can attach a short sampling corpus.

alyssa: perfect. If anyone hits customers affected by this regression, add them to the DOCS runbook and enable override for their nodes.

samir: I'll add telemetry events: `autotune.choice` with fields (kernel, measured_latency, model_score, driver_version, seqlen_bucket). Keeps things searchable.

alyssa: thanks team. If perf-bot confirms fallback on pool-a we can roll a hotfix to revert the last autotune model.

perf-bot: pool-a nodes currently 78% using tc path, ramping fallback in next 10m. Will post follow-up metrics. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
